page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The x86_64 architecture supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 support.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores placing the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation using Clang, ray tracing, and physics simulations. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET performance and static web serving throughput, fall within average ranges. Single-threaded gzip compression represents a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds for small and medium models are average, with prompt processing reaching 57.68 tokens/second on a 7B model.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores, high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and integrated NVMe SSD storage, this instance offers a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive workloads. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but the high RAM capacity and strong multi-core processing make it highly suitable for large-scale database hosting, software compilation pipelines, memory-cached web serving, and data processing tasks.
